note: Old Nettle, alone, because there is one of him. What he is worth is not what he pays: he pays nothing, and the argument for every number here is in the note beside him.

His walk is unhurried, because he has never once had to hurry, and his run is under the hero's 5.5 on purpose: he must never get away by being quicker than you. The only thing he ever gets away with is a decision you made.

One cut of the switch costs three out of ten hearts — under the ogre's four, because he is not strength — against half again the ogre's hit points, which makes him the longest fight in the game and means a hero who has not bothered with a decent blade simply does not finish it. He goes up a terrace exactly as the hero does, so the one free answer to an ogre is no answer here.
No gold and nothing to carry home. Every other kind pays out because every other kind can be finished; you never get so much as a moment to go through his coat.

One palette, where every other kind has three or four. Those exist so that a field of cows is not four copies of one cow. There is one of him, he is the same man in every village in the world, and a second palette would be a second person.
nettle.label: Old Nettle
lines: *he waits for you to come the last few yards*
"You are the one they sent, then."
*the switch goes back and forth, back and forth*
"We will both of us be here next spring."
